newsitem.title: USA: Maytag says Montgomery Ward owes $39 mln.
newsitem.headline: Maytag says Montgomery Ward owes $39 mln.

text.p: Maytag Corp, producer of major home appliances, floor care products and vending equipment, said it had accounts receivables of about $39 million due from retailer Montgomery Ward Holding Corp, which filed for bankruptcy July 7.
"It is too early to determine when and to what extent the amount due from Montgomery Ward will be recovered," said Maytag chairman and chief executive officer Leonard Hadley, in a news release.

"Based on information currently available, we have a reserve for the portion of this account we consider to be at risk. We continue to evaluate this situation and are having discussions with Montgomery Ward regarding our relationship as they restructure their business, operating under the auspices of bankruptcy court," Hadley added.

Earlier today, Maytag reported 1997 its second quarter sales rose 7.9 percent from the same period a year ago to $814.5 million and included $26.3 million in sales from a China joint venture formed last fall.
"Looking ahead, we continue to believe 1997 will be another good year for Maytag," Hadley said.
New products and models should help generate increased sales in the second half of this year, and some costs associated with the new product initiatives will decrease.

Maytag's second quarter earnings were $43.8 million or $0.45 a share compared with $44.3 million or $0.43 in the year ago quarter. Per share results in 1997 were based on about six percent fewer shares.

Sales of Hoover brand floor care products and Dixie-Narco vending equipment continued to be strong in the second quarter, and Maytag's commercial laundry equipment business benefited from launch of a horizontal-axis washer, it said.
Sales were up for Maytag International, which handles export sales and licensing agreements.
"Major appliances, our largest product category, posted a slight sales increase for the quarter in an intensely competitive business environment," Hadley said.

Sales of new Maytag and Jenn-Air brand refrigerators were exceptionally strong. Maytag laundry equipment and dishwashers, plus Magic Chef cooking appliances, also experienced quarterly gains in unit sales.
There was some weakness in other branded product categories and in private label sales, he noted.

As expected, operating income for major home appliances was somewhat depressed by costs associated with the initial production of new products, aggressive merchandising programs and added costs involving recently established regional product distribution centers, he said.
Shares of Maytag were trading off 1/8 to 27.
